title: Docker floating tags move only when the release is GitHub's canonical Latest release
answers: a patch release moved the Docker latest tag to an older version
why is docker latest not updated for maintenance releases
how are latest and latest-full image tags promoted in CI
release created with --latest=false changed the floating image tag
body:
Symptom: a maintenance patch release (published with `gh release create --latest=false`) moves Docker `latest`, `latest-full`, or model-server `latest` to an older image.
Root cause: .github/workflows/push-images.yml (the removed `check_latest` step) chose `latest` by semver-sorting `gh release list` output inside the image-build job, not by GitHub's Latest pointer.
Fix pattern: the build job pushes only versioned tags (`type=ref,event=tag`, `flavor: latest=false`). The `check-latest` job reads `gh api repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/latest --jq .tag_name` and compares it to the release tag. The `promote-latest` job re-checks that and then runs `docker buildx imagetools create` to retag the three floating images from the versioned ones.
Constraints: fail closed. A failed API read must leave promote=false and fail the job, and a mismatch must skip promotion. Do not reintroduce semver comparison or `type=raw,value=latest` in any metadata step.
applies: Changes to release-triggered image tagging and promotion in push-images.yml.
says: Publishing an older maintenance patch accidentally reverted our latest container image tag.
Prevent maintenance releases from updating the floating latest tag in the container registry.
Pulling the latest image tag downloads an older patch release instead of modern builds.
Only move the latest release tag when publishing the canonical newest platform version.
Backport releases published without the latest designation are erroneously retagging standard container images.
search: In .github/workflows/push-images.yml, build jobs push only versioned tags, while floating tags (latest, latest-full, and model-server latest) are promoted via docker buildx imagetools create only when check-latest matches GitHub's canonical latest release. The check-latest job reads gh api repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/latest --jq .tag_name to compare against the release tag, replacing semver sorting from gh release list that caused maintenance releases with --latest=false to retag floating images. Workflow failures must fail closed: a failed API call leaves promote=false and fails the job, mismatches skip promotion, and semver comparison or type=raw,value=latest must not be reintroduced.
